**Finding submitted: deviation (medium confidence, 0.72).**

Summary of the review:

- **Section 7.4 (Records; Inspection)** — the royalty audit the planner flagged — is **acceptable and not redlined**. It caps inspections at once each Calendar Year (one inspection per quarter), requires an independent nationally recognised accounting firm reasonably acceptable to us, obliges that Auditor to sign a confidentiality agreement, requires reasonable times and reasonable prior written notice, puts cost on Array absent an established underpayment above the (redacted) threshold, and gives no system access. The un-quantified notice period and the redacted percentage are noted in the rationale only.

- **Section 4.9(a) (Inspection Right)** is the real problem: a separate right for **Array itself** to enter our facilities and examine our internal procedures and records to verify compliance "with this Agreement," with **no frequency cap, no fixed notice period and no cost allocation**, plus an affirmative assistance obligation. Unlimited audits are walk-away territory under the rule, so I proposed the smallest edit reaching the preferred position — once in any twelve (12) month period, thirty (30) days' prior written notice, at Array's cost — mirroring the mechanics already conceded in Section 7.4, with 15 days offered as a fallback in the comment.
